newsitem.title: KENYA: Hutu rebel group says Burundi sanctions violated.
newsitem.headline: Hutu rebel group says Burundi sanctions violated.

text.p: A rebel group said on Saturday an Egyptian plane unloaded munitions and military uniforms at Burundi's capital Bujumbura on Friday in violation of regional sanctions.
The National Council for the Defence of Democracy (CNDD) made the accusation in a letter to the Tanzanian chairman of a regional committee monitoring sanctions imposed on Burundi last July.
It said the plane's manifest registered at Bujumbura airport listed it as flying from Ostend in Belgium to Lubumbashi, Zaire, on Thursday with 34 tonnes of cargo described as "Consolidation".

"This Egyptian plane arrived at Bujumbura international airport from Belgium on the night of December 26-27...The plane unloaded its cargo of 34 tonnes of tank/artillery pieces and left Bujumbura the same night at 3 a.m. after loading 24 tonnes of export tea.

"According to our information, the same plane is expected again in Bujumbura on the night between December 28-29. We hope this information will be of some use for you as chairman of the sanctions monitoring committee," CNDD said in a statement.
Lubumbashi in southeast Zaire is a major centre for Zairean government forces which are widely believed to be reinforcing for a counter-offensive against ethnic Tutsi rebels in eastern Zaire.
Regional states imposed economic sanctions on Burundi in July to force its new ruler Pierre Buyoya, who seized power in a coup by the Tutsi-dominated army, into peace talks with Hutu rebels.
CNDD's armed wing is the largest Hutu rebel group fighting in Burundi where more than 150,000 people have been killed in war and massacres since the killing of its first Hutu president in 1993.
